summary: This iRobot Create 3 Docs page gives network recommendations for communicating with the Create 3 robot from a computer or virtual machine. It covers supported Wi-Fi configurations and troubleshooting steps such as disabling multicasting, using a dedicated network, and the Fast DDS Discovery Server. It also explains Ethernet over USB setup with a static IP address and four VM networking options, with bridged networking recommended.
one_line: Network setup recommendations for connecting the iRobot Create 3 robot over Wi-Fi, Ethernet over USB, and virtual machines.
key_facts: Supported Wi-Fi authentication for the Create 3 robot is open (no password required) or shared key (password only).
Supported Wi-Fi frequency for the Create 3 robot is 2.4 GHz.
Both supported RMWs (Fast and Cyclone) require multicasting to be enabled on the Wi-Fi network by default.
The creators of Fast DDS recommend disabling multicasting when operating on a Wi-Fi network.
The Fast DDS Discovery Server further limits discovery traffic by routing discovery through a single server.
For Ethernet over USB, the USB/BLE toggle on the robot must be switched to the USB position.
For Ethernet over USB, the computer's wired connection should use IPv4 method manual with address 192.168.186.3 and netmask 255.255.0.0.
The iRobot Create 3 Webserver can be checked by navigating to 192.168.186.2 in a web browser when Ethernet over USB is working.
Option 1 (Recommended) for virtual machines is a bridged network connection; a shared or NAT connection will not allow ROS 2 to communicate with the Create 3 robot.
Option 2 for virtual machines is a USB Wi-Fi network adapter compatible with Ubuntu, assigned to the VM only.
With Option 2, the bridged connection between the VM and computer must be disconnected to avoid intermittent connection difficulties.
Option 3 (Advanced) involves assigning the VM the same MAC address as the computer's network adapter, which will likely result in loss of internet connection on the computer.
Option 4 (Advanced) is Ethernet over USB with the USB device assigned to the virtual machine as instructed in Option 3.
